answer: Hidden-Challenge Fork Test. The registry sends a shared random nonce to every identity and compares response hashes; two identities returning identical output are collapsed and lose registration. Each identity must keep a private kernel advanced by local entropy, so a clone cannot answer differently without independent state. Attackers pay one separate process, secret, and challenge-response run per identity, plus forfeiture on collision. A public terrace lists pending challenge slots. The ocean of unrelated identities supplies baseline response distributions for collision thresholds.
